content: Tetracycline is a yellow, odorless, crystalline powder. The drug's potency is compromised in solutions with a pH below 2, and it is rapidly degraded in the presence of alkali hydroxide solutions. Tetracycline exhibits very slight solubility in water, is freely soluble in dilute acids and alkali hydroxide solutions, sparingly soluble in alcohol, and practically insoluble in chloroform and ether. The chemical name of tetracycline hydrochloride is 4-(Dimethylamino)-1,4,4a,5,5a,6,11,12a-octahydro-3,6,10,12,-12a-pentahydroxy-6-methyl-1,11-dioxo-2-naphthacenecarboxamide monohydrochloride. Its structural formula is provided in the original documentation. Each oral capsule contains either 250 mg or 500 mg of tetracycline hydrochloride as the active ingredient. The inactive ingredients in the formulation include lactose, light mineral oil, and magnesium stearate. The capsule shells for both the 250 mg and 500 mg doses are composed of D&C Yellow No. 10, FD&C Blue No. 1, FD&C Yellow No. 6, gelatin, and titanium dioxide. The imprinting ink used on the capsules contains D&C Yellow No. 10, FD&C Blue No. 1, FD&C Blue No. 2, FD&C Red No. 40, iron oxide black, pharmaceutical shellac glaze, propylene glycol, and n-butyl alcohol.
